searchText: <schaliasos> re: **@tsahizid** > We will many times have multiple outgoing batch-posting transactions that could be included in the same block. We generally have 3 blobs per transaction. which rollup is this one? <thegaram33> has anyone managed to submit a transaction with 9 blobs? running into this issue, seems like a bug in geth blobpool validation https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/31792 <NicolasCsgy> re: **@thegaram33** > has anyone managed to submit a transaction with 9 blobs? running into this issue, seems like a bug in geth blobpool validation https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/31792 Asking to the geth team <thegaram33> re: **@thegaram33** > has anyone managed to submit a transaction with 9 blobs? running into this issue, seems like a bug in geth blobpool validation https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/31792 to avoid running into this I recommend that rollup teams set their max blob per tx count to 7 for now. <tsahizid> re: **@schaliasos** > which rollup is this one? Arbitrum. A tx with more than 3 blobs has a chance to find itself not included for a long time while blob price remains constant. <schaliasos> re: **@tsahizid** > Arbitrum. A tx with more than 3 blobs has a chance to find itself not included for a long time while blob price remains constant. but one transactions always submit just one batch, right? <tsahizid> re: **@schaliasos** > but one transactions always submit just one batch, right? Yes

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<tsahizid> re: **@schaliasos**
> which rollup is this one?
Arbitrum.
A tx with more than 3 blobs has a chance to find itself not included for a long time while blob price remains constant.
